title: Island
statementMd:
An ancient island suffered divine punishment, and the roads connecting its various regions were shattered.

The island can be regarded as an undirected graph containing $n$ vertices, numbered $1,2,\ldots,n$.

Initially, the roads on the island form an ordered rooted tree rooted at vertex $1$. The children of each vertex have a fixed left-to-right order, which is given in the input. In particular, the root has at least two children.

Starting from the root, perform a depth-first search, always recursively visiting the children of each vertex from left to right. Suppose there are $k$ leaf vertices. In the order in which they are first visited, they are $p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_k$. Here, a leaf vertex means a vertex of degree $1$; since the root has at least two children, it cannot be a leaf vertex.

Besides the $n-1$ roads in the tree, there are also $k-1$ roads built between consecutive leaves. For every $1\leq i \lt k$, the $i$-th road connects leaf vertex $p_i$ and leaf vertex $p_{i+1}$. That is, all leaves are connected consecutively into a chain in the above DFS order, and there are $n+k-2$ roads on the island in total.

When the divine punishment occurs, each road is independently destroyed with probability $\frac{1}{2}$, or retained with probability $\frac{1}{2}$, while all vertices still exist. The vertices and the remaining roads form several connected components. Let $X$ be the number of connected components of the island. Please calculate the expected value of $X$. Here a connected component is defined as a maximal connected subgraph. Note that an isolated vertex also counts as a component.

It can be proven that the answer is a rational number. Suppose the answer in lowest terms is $\frac{a}{b}$. You only need to output a nonnegative integer $x$ satisfying $0\leq x \lt 998244353$ and $bx\equiv a\pmod {998244353}$, namely, the answer modulo $998244353$.

## Input

The first line contains a positive integer $T$ $(1\leq T\leq 10^3)$, denoting the number of test cases.

For each test case, the first line contains an integer $n$ $(3\leq n\leq 10^5)$, denoting the number of vertices on the island.

The next $n$ lines describe the tree. The $i$-th line begins with an integer $c_i$ $(0\leq c_i \lt n,\sum c_i=n-1)$, denoting the number of children of vertex $i$. It is followed by $c_i$ pairwise distinct integers $e_{i,1},e_{i,2},\ldots,e_{i,c_i}$ $(2\leq e_{i,j}\leq n)$, giving the indices of all children of vertex $i$ in order.

It is guaranteed that, within a single test file, the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $3\times 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output one integer on one line, denoting the answer modulo $998244353$.

## Note

For the first test case, if vertices encountered again while backtracking are listed as well, the depth-first traversal starting from the root is:

$$ 1\to 2\to 1\to 3\to 1 $$

Thus, the leaves appear in the order $2,3$. Before the divine punishment, the island has the following three roads:

$$ (1,2),(1,3),(2,3) $$

The answer for the first test case is $\frac{13}{8}$.

For the second test case, the corresponding traversal order is:

$$ 1\to 6\to 1\to 2\to 4\to 2\to 5\to 2\to 1\to 3\to 1 $$

The leaves therefore appear in the order $6,4,5,3$. Before the divine punishment, the island has the following eight roads:

$$ (1,6),(1,2),(1,3),(2,4),(2,5),(6,4),(4,5),(5,3) $$

The answer for the second test case is $\frac{590}{256}=\frac{295}{128}$.
statementZhMd:
一座古老的岛屿遭受了神罚，连接岛上各个区域的道路遭到了破坏。

这座岛屿可以看作一张包含 $n$ 个顶点的无向图，顶点编号为 $1,2,\ldots,n$。

最初，岛上的道路构成一棵以顶点 $1$ 为根的有序有根树。每个顶点的子节点都有固定的从左到右的顺序，该顺序由输入给出。特别地，根节点至少有两个子节点。

从根节点开始进行深度优先搜索，每次都按照从左到右的顺序递归访问当前顶点的各个子节点。假设共有 $k$ 个叶子顶点，按照首次访问的顺序，它们依次为 $p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_k$。这里，叶子顶点指度数为 $1$ 的顶点；由于根节点至少有两个子节点，因此根节点不可能是叶子顶点。

除了树中的 $n-1$ 条道路外，相邻的叶子顶点之间还修建了 $k-1$ 条道路。对于每个 $1\leq i \lt k$，第 $i$ 条道路连接叶子顶点 $p_i$ 和叶子顶点 $p_{i+1}$。也就是说，所有叶子顶点按照上述 DFS 顺序依次连成一条链，岛上共有 $n+k-2$ 条道路。

神罚发生时，每条道路都独立地以 $\frac{1}{2}$ 的概率被摧毁，或以 $\frac{1}{2}$ 的概率被保留，而所有顶点仍然存在。所有顶点和剩余道路构成若干个连通分量。设 $X$ 为岛上的连通分量个数，请计算 $X$ 的期望值。这里，连通分量定义为极大连通子图。注意，孤立顶点也算作一个连通分量。

可以证明，答案是一个有理数。设答案的最简分数形式为 $\frac{a}{b}$。你只需输出一个非负整数 $x$，满足 $0\leq x \lt 998244353$ 且 $bx\equiv a\pmod {998244353}$，即答案对 $998244353$ 取模的结果。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个正整数 $T$ $(1\leq T\leq 10^3)$，表示测试用例的组数。

对于每组测试用例，第一行包含一个整数 $n$ $(3\leq n\leq 10^5)$，表示岛上的顶点个数。

接下来 $n$ 行描述这棵树。第 $i$ 行首先包含一个整数 $c_i$ $(0\leq c_i \lt n,\sum c_i=n-1)$，表示顶点 $i$ 的子节点个数。随后包含 $c_i$ 个两两不同的整数 $e_{i,1},e_{i,2},\ldots,e_{i,c_i}$ $(2\leq e_{i,j}\leq n)$，按顺序给出顶点 $i$ 的所有子节点的编号。

保证在同一个测试文件中，所有测试用例的 $n$ 之和不超过 $3\times 10^5$。

## 输出格式

对于每组测试用例，输出一行一个整数，表示答案对 $998244353$ 取模的结果。

## 说明

对于第一组测试用例，如果将回溯时再次经过的顶点也列出，那么从根节点开始的深度优先遍历顺序为：

$$ 1\to 2\to 1\to 3\to 1 $$

因此，叶子顶点的出现顺序为 $2,3$。神罚发生前，岛上有以下三条道路：

$$ (1,2),(1,3),(2,3) $$

第一组测试用例的答案为 $\frac{13}{8}$。

对于第二组测试用例，对应的遍历顺序为：

$$ 1\to 6\to 1\to 2\to 4\to 2\to 5\to 2\to 1\to 3\to 1 $$

因此，叶子顶点的出现顺序为 $6,4,5,3$。神罚发生前，岛上有以下八条道路：

$$ (1,6),(1,2),(1,3),(2,4),(2,5),(6,4),(4,5),(5,3) $$

第二组测试用例的答案为 $\frac{590}{256}=\frac{295}{128}$。
